tex_content.html:
Proposition

↗ lem:sum-sign-prod-det

(Cauchy–Binet formula.) Let $M$ and $N$ be matrices over $R$ with rows indexed by $\iota $ and columns by $\iota '$. Then \[ \sum _{s \colon \iota \to \iota '} \det \big(M[\, \cdot \, , s]\big)\, \det \big(N[\, \cdot \, , s]\big) = k!\, \det \big(MN^{T}\big), \] the sum running over all maps $s$, not only the injective or increasing ones.
Proof

↗ lem:sum-sign-prod-det Expanding both determinants by the Leibniz formula and multiplying,

\[ \det \big(M[\, \cdot \, , s]\big)\det \big(N[\, \cdot \, , s]\big) = \sum _{\sigma , \tau \in S_\iota } \operatorname {sgn}(\sigma )\operatorname {sgn}(\tau ) \prod _{i \in \iota } M_{\sigma (i)\, s(i)} N_{\tau (i)\, s(i)} . \]

Summing over $s$ and exchanging the sums, the inner sum over $s$ of a product over $i$ becomes a product over $i$ of sums over $\iota '$:

\[ \sum _{s \colon \iota \to \iota '} \prod _{i \in \iota } M_{\sigma (i)\, s(i)} N_{\tau (i)\, s(i)} = \prod _{i \in \iota } \sum _{m \in \iota '} M_{\sigma (i)\, m} N_{\tau (i)\, m} = \prod _{i \in \iota } (MN^{T})_{\sigma (i)\, \tau (i)} . \]

The result is now Lemma 5 applied to $C = MN^{T}$.

□

The classical statement of Cauchy--Binet sums over the $k$-element subsets $S \subseteq \iota '$ rather than over all maps. The two agree: a map $s$ that repeats a value selects a matrix with two equal columns, so it contributes $0$; and each injective $s$ with image $S$ is one of the $k!$ reindexings of the increasing enumeration of $S$, each contributing the same value because the two sign changes cancel.

The following generalization replaces the second determinant by an arbitrary alternating map. It is strictly stronger, since a determinant is an alternating function of the columns.
